findings.body: An unsupported nonempty pin is converted to an empty signoff, and migration continues after printing a warning. This weakens approval: approval.py:93 falls back to any accepted client-signoff record when the pin is empty. It also affects previously valid names such as docs/decisions/0001-acmeclient-signoff.md, which factory/scripts/factory_lib.py:532 accepts but the new SIGNOFF pattern rejects. A different accepted record can therefore satisfy approval after migration. Preserve supported legacy pins and refuse migration before making changes when a nonempty pin cannot be carried over.
findings.title: Preserve the sign-off gate when migration cannot carry its pin

findings.body: The new Unicode plan does not exercise UTF-8 stdin decoding. The hook helper at tests/test_story.py:106 serializes it with json.dumps(payload), whose default ensure_ascii=True escapes the arrow into ASCII. Removing stdin from cli.main's reconfiguration would therefore leave this test passing, despite its stated input-encoding coverage. Send the payload with ensure_ascii=False under the forced ASCII environment and assert that approval succeeds.
findings.title: Not done: UTF-8 hook-input regression test

findings.body: Using next() assigns each reported check to only one requirement. With checks = ["tests", "tests (windows-latest)"], a successful Windows run is assigned to "tests", leaving the explicitly named Windows requirement empty. Close then times out claiming it has not reported even when every check passed. The previous per-requirement matching handled this configuration. Evaluate presence and success for every matching required name while retaining the new checks for unnamed jobs.
findings.title: Count a check toward every matching required name
